content:
## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `addpipe32` (32-bit registered adder: y = a + b (mod 2^32)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;

        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= a_i + b_i;
    end
end

endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 671.384 um^2, WNS 7.57073 ns, estimated score 75.035916 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: Manual arithmetic restructuring (carry-select variants) consistently produced worse estimated WNS and only marginal area savings, suggesting the default Yosys/ABC synthesis already produces a well-optimized (near carry-lookahead) structure for the 32-bit adder that my manual restructuring only hindered by adding extra mux overhead. Let me verify the original spec RTL directly with the full place-and-route flow to confirm its real score, since none of my attempted rewrites beat the baseline estimate.

I explored several alternative adder architectures (16+16 carry-select, 4-way 8-bit carry-select) via the cheap `estimate_ppa` tool, but all of them produced worse timing (lower WNS ~7.39-7.40ns vs baseline 7.57ns) despite modest area savings, because the default Yosys/ABC synthesis flow already restructures the plain `a+b` expression into a well-optimized fast-adder netlist automatically — my manual restructuring only added extra multiplexer overhead on the critical path without reducing logic depth. I also confirmed that RTL style variations that are logically identical (separate always blocks, if/else restructuring) synthesize to the exact same netlist and give identical estimates, confirming the front-end already normalizes such changes. Since none of the alternatives beat the original specification's post-route score (area 746.13 um², WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607, verified via `place_and_route`), I'm concluding that the given specification RTL is already at or very near the practical optimum achievable within this synthesis/PnR flow for this small, latency-fixed pipelined adder, and further experimentation is unlikely to yield gains given the remaining budget.

input.summary: Investigated multiple RTL restructurings of the addpipe32 32-bit pipelined adder to improve post-route score (10*WNS - 0.001*area). Tried: (1) 16+16-bit carry-select adder, (2) 4-way 8-bit carry-select adder, (3) equivalent behavioral rewrites (separate always blocks, if/else restructuring). All logically-equivalent rewrites that didn't change the arithmetic structure synthesized to an identical netlist (671.384 um^2, 7.57073 ns estimated WNS), confirming Yosys/ABC's front-end normalization. The manual carry-select variants, intended to shorten the critical carry chain, instead produced worse estimated timing (WNS ~7.39-7.40 ns vs baseline 7.57 ns) with only marginal area reduction, indicating ABC's default technology mapping already restructures the plain `a_i + b_i` expression into a near-optimal fast-adder network, and manual carry-select muxing only added extra delay overhead. Since no candidate improved on the original specification's measured place-and-route result (area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607, verified this run), I confirmed that result via place_and_route and am finishing with the original specification RTL as the best verified design, since it already matches the practical optimum achievable through this synthesis/PnR flow for this simple, latency-fixed pipelined adder.
